Which of these is a responsibility of ev: Respecting the rights of others, including their right to their own opinions, is one of the responsibilities the handbook expects of everyone living in the UK.
Which of these is a listed responsibilit: Looking after yourself and your family is one of the listed responsibilities, along with obeying the law, treating others fairly and caring for your area and the environment.
Which TWO are rights shared by everyone: Freedom of speech and a right to a fair trial are both shared rights, along with freedom of belief, freedom from unfair discrimination, and the right to join in electing a government.
Which TWO must citizenship applicants de: Applicants must be able to speak and read English and show a good understanding of life in the UK, which is what this test assesses.
To whom is the oath of allegiance made?: The oath of allegiance is sworn to the monarch, their heirs and successors. Those who prefer not to swear by God make a solemn affirmation instead.
How many countries make up the UK?: The UK is made up of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
Which TWO languages other than English a: Welsh is spoken in Wales and Gaelic in parts of Scotland. Irish Gaelic and Ulster Scots are spoken in Northern Ireland.
Which TWO crosses appear on the Union Fl: The Union Flag combines the crosses of St George for England, St Andrew for Scotland and St Patrick for Ireland. Wales is not represented.
Parts of which Roman structure can still: Hadrian's Wall was built across northern England on the orders of Emperor Hadrian, and long stretches of it survive today.
Which of these peoples settled in Britai: The Angles, Saxons and Jutes came from northern Europe after the Romans left. England takes its name from the Angles.
The name England derives from which of t: England takes its name from the Angles, one of the peoples who settled in Britain after the Romans left.
Which TWO of these are associated with t: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 brought the Normans to power, and the Domesday Book was compiled in 1086 to record who held what.
Complete the sentence: the Norman Conque: William of Normandy defeated Harold at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, the last successful foreign invasion of England.
Who led the Norman invasion of England?: William of Normandy led the invasion, defeated Harold at Hastings in 1066, and became known as William the Conqueror.
In which year was the Great Charter sign: Magna Carta, the Great Charter, was agreed by King John in 1215 and established that even the king was subject to the law.
When did the Roman conquest of Britain b: The Romans invaded successfully in AD 43 under Emperor Claudius. Julius Caesar's earlier attempt in 55 BC had failed.
The Victorian era ended in which year?: Queen Victoria reigned from 1837 until her death in 1901, more than 60 years.
When did the Channel finally separate Br: Britain was joined to the continent by a land bridge until about 10,000 years ago, when rising seas made it an island.
Which German ruler became King George I: George I was the German Elector of Hanover, chosen as the nearest Protestant relative of Queen Anne. He spoke little English and relied on his ministers.
Which minister led the creation of the N: Aneurin Bevan, Minister for Health in Clement Attlee's Labour government, led the creation of the NHS in 1948.
Who developed a vaccination against smal: Edward Jenner, working in Gloucestershire, developed a vaccination against smallpox in the 1790s.
Who developed the theory of evolution by: Charles Darwin set out the theory of evolution by natural selection in On the Origin of Species, published in 1859.
The suffragette movement was led by whom: Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women's Social and Political Union, whose members became known as suffragettes.
Which TWO periods came before the Romans: The Bronze Age and Iron Age both preceded the Roman invasion of AD 43. Iron Age people built hill forts and minted the first British coins.
Which TWO peoples settled in Britain aft: The Angles and Saxons came from northern Europe, along with the Jutes, after the Roman army withdrew in AD 410.
Which TWO events took place in the Middl: Magna Carta was agreed in 1215 and the Black Death reached England in 1348, killing about a third of the population.
Which TWO of these were medieval English: Henry V won at Agincourt in 1415, and Richard III was killed at Bosworth Field in 1485, ending the Wars of the Roses.
Which TWO figures are associated with Br: Admiral Nelson won at Trafalgar in 1805, where he was killed, and the Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815.
Which TWO people campaigned against the: The Quakers formed the first anti-slavery groups, and William Wilberforce led the campaign in Parliament. The trade was banned in 1807.
Which TWO were created by the post-war L: Clement Attlee's Labour government, elected in 1945, created the National Health Service in 1948 and the modern welfare state.
Which TWO British inventors worked on fl: Sir Frank Whittle developed the jet engine in the 1930s, and Sir Robert Watson-Watt developed radar, which helped detect incoming aircraft in the war.
Which TWO of these British achievements: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989, and Crick and Watson discovered the structure of DNA in 1953.
Which TWO of these happened during the S: Over 300,000 troops were evacuated from Dunkirk in 1940, and the RAF won the Battle of Britain in the summer of the same year.
Which TWO of these events happened in th: The Scottish independence referendum was held in 2014 and the UK left the European Union in 2020. The NHS was founded in 1948 and the Battle of Britain fought in 1940.
Which of these dishes is traditionally a: Welsh cakes are a traditional Welsh dish. Haggis is Scottish, the Ulster fry comes from Northern Ireland, and roast beef with Yorkshire pudding is English.
Which of these best describes the UK tod: The UK is an increasingly diverse society, with people of many different cultures, backgrounds and religions living together.
What do the letters BAFTA stand for?: BAFTA stands for the British Academy of Film and Television Arts, which runs the UK's main film awards.
Which of these is a famous castle in Wal: Caernarfon Castle in north Wales is one of the ring of castles built by Edward I to hold Wales after his conquest.
Which of these is a well-known British c: Sir Edward Elgar is best known for the Pomp and Circumstance Marches, the first of which is sung as Land of Hope and Glory.
Which author wrote Great Expectations?: Charles Dickens wrote Great Expectations and Oliver Twist, novels about social conditions in Victorian Britain.
Which author wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four?: George Orwell wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four and Animal Farm, both reflecting on politics and power.
Who designed the Houses of Parliament?: Sir Charles Barry designed the Houses of Parliament in the Gothic style, after the old palace burned down in 1834.
Psycho and The Birds were directed by wh: Sir Alfred Hitchcock directed Psycho and The Birds and was a leading figure in British and American cinema.
People rent allotments in order to do wh: An allotment is a small plot of land rented for growing vegetables and flowers, popular with people who have no garden of their own.
Which TWO are traditionally associated w: Bonfires and fireworks mark 5 November, remembering the failure of the Gunpowder Plot of 1605.
Which TWO events are held annually in th: The Wimbledon Championships is the oldest tennis tournament in the world, and the Grand National is a steeplechase run at Aintree.
Which TWO novels were written by the Bro: Charlotte Bronte wrote Jane Eyre and her sister Emily wrote Wuthering Heights.
How frequently is the population of the: A census of the UK population is taken every 10 years, and the detailed information is made public after 100 years.
Which of these describes religious freed: The UK is a tolerant society: everyone may practise a religion, change it, or have no religion at all.
In which sport did Sir Ian Botham repres: Sir Ian Botham captained the English cricket team and held records for both runs scored and wickets taken.
In which sport did Jayne Torvill and Chr: Torvill and Dean won Olympic gold for ice dancing in 1984 and were world champions four times.
Which author wrote Far from the Madding: Thomas Hardy wrote Far from the Madding Crowd and other novels set in the rural south-west of England.
Which author created the character of Ja: Ian Fleming wrote the James Bond novels, which have been filmed in Britain since the 1960s.
Which author is famous for detective nov: Agatha Christie is the best-known British author of detective fiction, and her novels have sold worldwide.
Which flower show held in London is know: The Chelsea Flower Show is held in London each year and reflects the British enthusiasm for gardening.
The rock formation on the north-east coa: The Giant's Causeway is a volcanic rock formation on the north-east coast of Northern Ireland and a World Heritage Site.
Which observation wheel stands on the So: The London Eye is a giant observation wheel on the South Bank of the Thames, built to mark the millennium.
Which charity preserves historic buildin: The National Trust, founded in 1895, is a charity that preserves important buildings, coastline and countryside.
What happens when an MP dies or resigns: A by-election is held in that constituency to elect a new MP.
What do the initials PCSO stand for?: PCSO stands for Police Community Support Officer. They work alongside police officers and have different powers from them.
Which of these is a way of helping to pr: Recycling household waste helps protect the environment, as do walking or cycling short journeys and shopping locally.
How many people sit on a Scottish jury?: A jury in Scotland has 15 members. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland a jury has 12.
Which TWO chambers make up the UK Parlia: Parliament consists of the House of Commons, whose 650 members are elected, and the House of Lords, whose members are appointed.
How many jurors hear a Crown Court trial: Serious criminal cases in England and Wales are heard in the Crown Court before a judge and a jury of 12.
Which TWO are civic duties of residents: Obeying the law and serving on a jury when called are both civic duties expected of residents in the UK.
What is the minimum voting age in the UK: You can vote in a UK general election at 18, provided you are on the electoral register and eligible.
The UK system of government is described: The UK is a constitutional monarchy: the monarch is Head of State but does not rule, and the country is governed by ministers accountable to an elected Parliament.
Which TWO of these are senior government: The Chancellor of the Exchequer runs the economy and the Home Secretary is responsible for crime, policing and immigration.
The Treasury is led by which minister?: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is responsible for the economy and lives at 11 Downing Street.
Which of these actions breaks UK equalit: Discriminating against someone because of their disability is unlawful, as is discrimination on grounds of race, sex, religion, age or sexual orientation.
Which TWO roles does the Prime Minister: The Prime Minister is Head of Government and appoints the Cabinet of about 20 senior ministers. The monarch is Head of State.
Which TWO taxes or contributions do most: Most workers pay income tax, usually deducted through PAYE, and National Insurance contributions, which fund state benefits and the State Pension.
